# CEO-01→12 — Founder/CEO Executive Development (external/market, EXECUTIVE_ONLY)

## Grounding

Per `FOUNDER_CEO_GROUP_FONDATION_RECONCILIATION.md`: coverage `NONE`,
distinctness `DISTINCT_PROFESSION` for all 12 — founder-to-CEO
transition, executive team-building, board/investor communication,
delegation, institutionalization/succession is a well-established
executive-development genre (the same territory as YPO/Vistage-style
peer-executive curricula). Action: `NEW_EXTERNAL` for all 12,
`EXECUTIVE_ONLY` context preserved from the source — a **governance
control on who can access the content** (gated to founder/CEO-level
learners), never a content-design constraint.

## Objectives

Teach the real, current executive-development disciplines this
cluster covers, as market-general leadership knowledge, without
inventing jurisdiction-specific legal or fiscal content — none of
these 12 titles require a corporate-law or tax claim to teach honestly:

- Founder-to-CEO identity transition.
- Executive team-building and delegation.
- Board and investor communication.
- Institutionalization and succession planning.

## Modules

1. Founder-to-CEO identity and role transition.
2. Executive team-building.
3. Delegation and letting-go-of-execution discipline.
4. Board communication and governance literacy (market-general —
   never a substitute for jurisdiction-specific corporate-law content,
   which stays out of scope here per `GRP-11`'s own
   `NEEDS_EXPERT_REVIEW` boundary in `docs/grp/`).
5. Investor communication and fundraising narrative.
6. Institutionalization — building process that outlives the founder.
7. Succession planning.
8. Boundary discipline — this cluster never claims a corporate-law,
   tax, or fiduciary-duty capability; any candidate requiring
   jurisdiction-specific legal/fiscal content is out of scope here and
   handled, where it exists in this domain family, as
   `NEEDS_EXPERT_REVIEW` (see `docs/grp/NEEDS_EXPERT_REVIEW.md`,
   `docs/fdc/NEEDS_EXPERT_REVIEW.md`).

## Assessment

An executive-development literacy exam graded against real
peer-executive-curriculum practice, with an eliminatory check on
asserting jurisdiction-specific corporate-law, tax, or fiduciary
content as if it were market-general.
